originality.rationale: Targeted successful semantic searches and direct statement-level inspection of both a 1999 full primary design-coloring paper and a 2018 full primary hypergraph recoloring paper found no statement that covers the exact finite Fano weak-coloring reconfiguration graph. The known order-seven (4,2,1) bicoloring split is only a strict-state-space existence fact; the random-hypergraph theorem does not apply with its quantitative assumptions. Several other plausible abstracts were compared, and accessible historical claims excluded overlap. This is a best-knowledge same-model originality finding; some less accessible full texts and unindexed finite tables remain residual risks. In the order-seven model, exactly the 126 weak colorings with class profile (1,2,4) satisfy the earlier stricter bicoloring constraint; all remaining 756 weak states fall outside it.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished finite enumerations could include the same numbers or graph.
Older 1982 Steiner-coloring and 2014 two-coloring papers were not fully accessible in the consulted materials.
The later journal version of Anastos–Frieze was assessed against a full related preprint plus journal abstract rather than full journal text.

value.rationale: Weak three-coloring is the natural chromatic threshold of the seven-point Fano plane, not an arbitrary finite slice. The exact connected solution-space geometry, sharp all-pair \(d\le h+1\) theorem, finite exceptional-pair census and automorphism orbit classification quantify a genuine recoloring obstruction and yield a reproducible baseline for hypergraph-coloring dynamics. No unmotivated infinite extrapolation or promised downstream theorem is needed.
